paper_metadata.title: Encoding trade-offs and design toolkits in quantum algorithms for discrete optimization: coloring, routing, scheduling, and other problems

experiments.description: Numerical study of encoding choice for diagonal primitives and penalties by compiling exact exponentials of DQIR operators across multiple encodings and variable cardinalities.

algorithm.variant: Exact exponentiation of diagonal DQIR primitives and penalties via product formulas / Pauli Frame Graph compilation

problem_formulation.objective_function: Exact exponentials of diagonal operators including EQ, A_n, A_n^2, F_perm, F_sum, and F_SS
problem_formulation.problem_hamiltonian: Diagonal Hamiltonians derived from DQIR primitives and penalties

problem_instance.description: Abstract benchmark over DQIR primitives and penalties, not a single application instance

quantum_resources.circuit_depth: Reported and compared across encodings; exact numeric depths shown in Figure 9 but not enumerated in text

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: DQIR construction, algebraic simplification, encoding selection, Pauli conversion, PFG-based ordering

experiments.description: Numerical study of encoding choice for full cost functions in graph coloring, scheduling, routing/TSP, and portfolio rebalancing by compiling exact exponentials of the cost Hamiltonians.

algorithm.variant: Exact exponentiation of cost Hamiltonians for AQO/QAOA-style phase operators

objective_function: Graph coloring: sum over edges of EQ(x_alpha, x_beta)
TSP: sum over consecutive cities d(tau(a), tau(a+1))
Machine scheduling: total weighted lateness using start-time operators
Portfolio rebalancing: lambda z^T Sigma z - (1-lambda) mu^T z + trading cost
constraints_handling: Permutation penalties or permutation-preserving mixers for TSP and scheduling
F_sum penalty for portfolio rebalancing constraint sum z_alpha = D
Variable-domain penalties for invalid encodings in graph coloring
problem_hamiltonian: HC = sum_(alpha,beta in E) EQ(x_alpha, x_beta)
HC = sum_alpha sum_k sum_l<k d(k,l) P_alpha^(k) P_(alpha+1)^(l)
HC = lambda sum_{alpha,beta} sigma_{alpha beta} A_alpha A_beta - (1-lambda) sum_alpha mu_alpha A_alpha + trading cost

problem_instance.description: Toy benchmark instances used to compare encoding-dependent circuit depths; graph coloring uses complete graphs with number of nodes equal to number of colors d; portfolio rebalancing uses d=3; scheduling and TSP are permutation problems with varying d

dataset_specification.description: Synthetic benchmark instances; graph coloring uses complete graphs; portfolio rebalancing follows the model of Hodson et al. with d=3

quantum_resources.circuit_depth: Reported in Figure 10; exact numeric depths not enumerated in text

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: DQIR construction, encoding selection, Pauli conversion, PFG-based ordering

experiments.description: Numerical study of approximate single-variable mixers obtained by first-order product-formula decomposition of the shift mixer Hamiltonian.

algorithm.variant: Approximate shift mixer (leaky) for single-variable QAOA
algorithm.ansatz: QAOA mixer layer based on exp(-i theta G_shift)

problem_formulation.objective_function: Mixer-only benchmark; no problem objective beyond implementing the shift Hamiltonian

problem_instance.description: Abstract single-variable mixer benchmark over discrete domains of size d

quantum_resources.circuit_depth: Reported in Figure 11 (left); exact numeric depths not enumerated in text

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: PFG-based compilation of the product formula

experiments.description: Numerical study of strict graph-derived partial mixers (GDPMs) for single-variable domains across standard binary, Gray, and block-unary encodings.

algorithm.variant: Strict single-variable GDPMs designed by graph search
algorithm.ansatz: Exact mixer circuits built from multi-controlled Pauli-Y rotations and related gates

hyperparameters.variable_cardinality_range: d up to 15 for SB and Gray; BU example shown for g=3

problem_instance.description: Abstract single-variable mixer benchmark for d-level variables; figures show d=3,5,6,7,9,10,11,12,13,14,15 and special power-of-two cases

quantum_resources.circuit_depth: Reported in Figure 11 (right); exact numeric depths not enumerated in text

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Graph search over a library of partial mixers; decomposition using known gate synthesis results

experiments.description: Numerical study of strict graph-derived partial permutation mixers (PPMs) for permutation problems, especially routing and scheduling, using Gray-code constructions up to d=16.

algorithm.variant: Strict permutation GDPM / partial permutation mixer
algorithm.ansatz: Two-variable partial permutation mixers built from A_phi-type gates

design_criteria: no edges between good and bad states

problem_instance.description: Abstract two-variable permutation benchmark; examples shown for d=5 and generalization up to d=16

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Graph-theoretic mixer design; optional Gray-to-standard-binary conversion
